# Reductivity of a group generated by rank-one line pairs

This internal derived support module, in namespace
`Langlands.GroupScheme.MaximalSplitSubgroup`, is part of the proof of
`MaximalSplitSubgroupStatement` (Borel–Tits 1965, Theorem 7.2). It proves, over an
algebraically closed field, that a group generated by a split torus and pairs of
opposite lines is connected reductive with a prescribed root set. This is the
reductive case of Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive groups*, Theorem C.2.29
(parts (ii), (iv) and (v)), proved by a different route (see Provenance).

The setting is the one of the companion modules `MaximalSplitGeneratedCell`,
`MaximalSplitGeneratedWeights` and `MaximalSplitGeneratedMultiplicity`. `T` is a
commutative group scheme over `Spec k`, `H` a group scheme over `Spec k`,
`t : T.toGrp ⟶ H` a homomorphism, and `x i`, `y i : Ga k ⟶ H` (for `i` in an index
type `Idx`) lines of weights `a i` and `-a i`
(`VectorGroup.IsTorusEquivariant t (x i) (a i)`, and likewise for `y i`). `RelationOver
t ν x y Z` is the Library's rank-one relation `x(X) y(Y) = y(Y') ν(u) x(X')` for all
points `X, Y` over `Z` with `u = 1 + XY` a unit, `X' = u⁻¹X`, `Y' = u⁻¹Y`. `cone a` is
the additive subsemigroup generated by the `a i` (from `MaximalSplitGeneratedWeights`).

## Declarations

- `crd_inv`: the coordinate of the inverse of a point `b` of `Ga k` is `-crd b`.
- `pt_neg_crd`: the point of `Ga k` with coordinate `-crd b` is `b⁻¹`.
- `coU_neg`: the point `ν'(u)` of `H`, for the opposite cocharacter `ν' = -ν`, is the
  inverse of `ν(u)` (both followed by `t`).
- `relationOver_swap`: `RelationOver t ν x y Z` implies `RelationOver t (-ν) y x Z`,
  that is, `y(X) x(Y) = x(Y') ν(u)⁻¹ y(X')` under the same conditions.
- `neg_mem_cone_of_mem_cone_neg`: if `χ` lies in the cone of the family `-a i`, then
  `-χ` lies in the cone of the `a i`.
- `LiesInReflectionClosure a ν Φ'` (definition): every character in `Φ'` satisfies
  every predicate `P` on characters that holds at each `a i` and is preserved by each
  map `χ ↦ χ - ⟨χ, ν i⟩ • a i`. In words, `Φ'` lies in the smallest set containing
  the `a i` and stable under these reflections.

The remaining declarations assume that `k` is algebraically closed, that `H` is
smooth and affine over `Spec k` (`[Smooth H.X.hom]`, `[IsAffineHom H.X.hom]`), that
`T` is split, and the generation hypotheses of `mem_cone_of_mem_relativeRoots`:
`RelationOver t (ν i) (x i) (y i)` over the base point, `x i` commutes with `y j` (on
rational points) for `i ≠ j`, the subgroup generated by the rational points of the
lines and of `t` has dense image in `H`, a cocharacter `cch` pairs positively with
every `a i`, and `t` is a closed subgroup.

- `neg_mem_cone_of_mem_roots`: a root `χ` of `t` with `⟨χ, cch⟩ < 0` has
  `-χ ∈ cone a`.
- `mem_cone_or_neg_mem_cone_of_mem_roots`: a root `χ` with `⟨χ, cch⟩ ≠ 0` satisfies
  `χ ∈ cone a` or `-χ ∈ cone a`.
- `isWeylLineRoot_line`: suppose in addition that `eta` isolates the index `i`
  (`IsIsolatingCocharacter a i eta`), `x i` is a monomorphism, `⟨a i, ν i⟩ = 2`, and a
  rational point `n` of `H` normalizes `t` through the lattice reflection
  `latticeReflectionIso (a i) (ν i) hpair`. Then `IsWeylLineRoot t (a i)`: `a i` is a
  root, its weight space is one-dimensional, and it has a Weyl inversion.
- `isConnectedReductive_and_roots_eq_of_generated`: assume moreover that `H` is
  connected, and for every `i`: `x i` is a monomorphism, some cocharacter isolates
  `i`, `⟨a i, ν i⟩ = 2`, and some rational point normalizes `t` through the reflection
  `latticeReflectionIso (a i) (ν i)`. Assume `⟨χ, cch⟩ ≠ 0` for every root `χ`. Let
  `Φ'` be a set of characters such that
  - every root `χ` with `χ ∈ cone a` or `-χ ∈ cone a` lies in `Φ'`,
  - `Φ'` is reduced: if `α, β ∈ Φ'` and `m • β = n • α` with integers `m ≠ 0`, then
    `β = α` or `β = -α`,
  - `LiesInReflectionClosure a ν Φ'`.

  Then `H` is connected reductive (`IsConnectedReductive H`) and `roots t = Φ'`.

## Proofs

`crd_inv` is `map_inv` for the coordinate isomorphism of `Ga`. `pt_neg_crd` follows by
injectivity of `crd`. `coU_neg`: the group homomorphism of `-ν` is the pointwise
inverse of that of `ν`, and composition with a group homomorphism commutes with
inversion.

`relationOver_swap`: given `X, Y, X', Y', u` as in the relation for `y, x`, apply the
relation for `x, y` to `-Y, -X, -Y', -X'` and the same `u`; the side conditions hold
since `1 + (-Y)(-X) = 1 + XY`. By `pt_neg_crd` it reads
`x(Y)⁻¹ y(X)⁻¹ = y(X')⁻¹ ν(u) x(Y')⁻¹`. Inverting both sides gives
`y(X) x(Y) = x(Y') ν(u)⁻¹ y(X')`, and `coU_neg` rewrites `ν(u)⁻¹` as `(-ν)(u)`.

`neg_mem_cone_of_mem_cone_neg` is induction on the additive closure.

`neg_mem_cone_of_mem_roots` applies `mem_cone_of_mem_relativeRoots` to the swapped
data: the lines `y i` of weights `-a i`, the lines `x i` of weights `-(-a i)`, the
cocharacters `-ν i` with `relationOver_swap`, the cocharacter `-cch`, the commutation
hypothesis with indices exchanged, and the same generated subgroup (the union
reordered). The Library's `relativeRoots_eq_roots` identifies relative roots with
roots. It gives `χ ∈ cone (fun i => -a i)`, and `neg_mem_cone_of_mem_cone_neg`
concludes. `mem_cone_or_neg_mem_cone_of_mem_roots` splits on the sign of `⟨χ, cch⟩`.

`isWeylLineRoot_line`: `finrank_weightSpace_eq_one` (from
`MaximalSplitGeneratedMultiplicity`) gives the one-dimensional weight space. So the
weight space is nonzero, and `a i ≠ 0` since `⟨a i, cch⟩ > 0`; hence `a i` is a root
(`mem_roots`). The Weyl inversion is `hasWeylInversion_of_reflection` from
`MaximalSplitGeneratedWeyl`.

`isConnectedReductive_and_roots_eq_of_generated`: by `isWeylLineRoot_line` each `a i`
satisfies `IsWeylLineRoot t`. This predicate is preserved by every reflection
`χ ↦ χ - ⟨χ, ν i⟩ • a i` (`IsWeylLineRoot.reflection` with the normalizing point of
index `i`). By `LiesInReflectionClosure` every element of `Φ'` satisfies it, so
`Φ' ⊆ roots t`. Conversely every root lies in `cone a` or its negative by
`mem_cone_or_neg_mem_cone_of_mem_roots`, hence in `Φ'`. So `roots t = Φ'`. Reductivity
is the criterion `RootwiseWeyl.isConnectedReductive_of_rootwiseWeyl` (module
`Reductive.RootwiseWeylReductivity`). Its
hypotheses are: the torus centralizer is `t` itself (`torusCentralizer_eq_range_of_generated`
from `MaximalSplitGeneratedCell`), one-dimensional root spaces and Weyl inversions
(from `IsWeylLineRoot`, the latter through `HasWeylInversion.exists_transporter`),
and reducedness of the roots (the hypothesis on `Φ'`, since `roots t = Φ'`).

## Provenance

Derived. CGP Theorem C.2.29 (printed pp. 625–628, PDF pp. 651–654) treats a group `F`
generated by rank-one groups `F_a`, `a ∈ Δ`, around a common centralizer `C` of a split
torus `S`. Part (ii) (Step 1) puts the nonzero weights of `S` on `Lie(F)` into
`A⁺ ∪ A⁻`, the semigroups generated by `±Δ`; parts (iv)–(v) (Steps 3–4) show that `F`
is reductive when every `F_a` is. Step 3 fixes points `n_a ∈ F_a(k)` normalizing `S`
and acting on `X(S)` by the reflections `r_a`, and uses that the weights on a
normal subgroup's Lie algebra are stable under the Weyl group they generate.

The formal proof keeps the inputs (lines `x i = E_{a}`, `y i = E_{-a}` with the
rank-one relation, normalizing points acting by reflections) but argues reductivity
differently. CGP derive a contradiction from a weight of the unipotent radical. Here
the roots are matched with the given set `Φ'`: the inclusion `roots t ⊆ Φ'` comes from
part (ii) through `hsub`, and `Φ' ⊆ roots t` from Weyl transport of the simple roots
`a i`, as in Step 3. Each root then has a one-dimensional weight space and a Weyl
inversion, which is the input of the companion criterion
`RootwiseWeyl.isConnectedReductive_of_rootwiseWeyl`. The set `Φ'`, its reducedness and
reflection-closure hypotheses, and the generic cocharacter `cch` are hypotheses of
this module; the caller supplies them. The definition `LiesInReflectionClosure` is a
local packaging of the reflection-closure hypothesis. No statement is assumed.
